narrative:
The model estimates a 71% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key aspects of your profile that, according to patterns seen across many similar employees, strongly signal higher turnover risk.

Your total years of experience is the most influential factor. With over 11 years of overall professional experience, you stand out from the majority of employees the model expects to stay, who typically have far less (only 14.7% of stayers have 11+ years). Longer overall careers appear to make people more likely to explore new opportunities elsewhere.

Next, the length of time you have spent in your current role also pushes the prediction toward leaving. Having been at this organization for only 1–5 years places you in the most common group among those predicted to leave, whereas longer tenure in the current job is more typical of people expected to remain.

Finally, the fact that you have not received other job offers while working here actually works in your favor and pulls the prediction slightly back toward staying. Most employees the model thinks will stay also report no external offers, so this is a stabilizing element.

Taken together, your extensive overall experience and relatively short time in this specific role outweighed the positive effect of having no outside offers, leading to the decision to deny the promotion. The organization should discuss retention strategies with you, such as faster career progression or improved work conditions, while you may wish to reflect on whether your long-term goals still align with staying.
